questions.q: In $\mathrm{SOCl}_2$ the $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{O}$ bond angle are
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{SOCl}_2$ has one $\mathrm{S}=0$ double bond and two $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{Cl}$ single bond.
Hybridisation of $S=\frac{1}{2}[6+2-0+0]=4$
Thus, $S$ is $s p^3$. Since, $\mathrm{SOCl}_2$ has only three sigma bond, therefore it has one lone pair of electrons on $S$ atom and hence its shape is pyramidal and the bond angle are less than $109.5^{\circ}$ due to repulsion between lone pairs.
Further, since $\pi$-electrons of the $\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{O}$ bonds are more polarised, therefore, they repel the bond pair of $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond.
Thus, making $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{O}$ bond larger than $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond angle.

$\left[\right.$ Given $E_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}}^{\circ}=0.34 \mathrm{~V}, E_{\mathrm{Sn}^{2+} / / \mathrm{sn}}^{\circ}=-0.14 \mathrm{~V}F=96500 \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{mol}]$

Given,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{Cu}(s)+\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M})+\mathrm{Sn}(s) \\ \\ & E_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}=E_{\text {cathode }}^{\circ}-E_{\text {anoode }}^{\circ} \\ \\ & =-0.14-(0.34)=-0.48 \mathrm{~V} \\ \\ & E_{\text {cell }}=E_{\text {cell }}^*-\frac{0.059}{n} \log \frac{\left[\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]}[n=2] \\ \\ & =-0.48-\frac{0.059}{2} \log \frac{[0.1]}{0.01} \\ \\ & =-0.48-0.0290 \log [10]=-0.5095 \mathrm{~V} \\ \end{aligned}$
Gibb's free energy,
$\begin{aligned} \\ \Delta G & =-n F E_{\text {cell }} \\ \\ & =+2(96500) \times 0.5095 \\ \\ & =98.33 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol} \\ \end{aligned}$
or $983 \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$
Hence, the value of $x$ is 983 .

Given,
Density of KCl solution $=1.20 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mL}$
Molality of solution $=6.60 \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{kg}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{KCl}=74.5$
Molality $=\frac{6.60 \mathrm{~mol}}{\mathrm{~kg}}=\frac{6.60 \mathrm{~mol} \text { solute }}{1000 \mathrm{~g} \text { solvant }}$

$\begin{aligned} \\ \text { So, molarity } & =\frac{6.60 \times 1.2}{1491.7} \times 1000 \\ \\ M & =5.3 \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L} \\ \end{aligned}$
Nearest integer $=5 \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}$

In a closed vessel, 5 moles of $A_2(g)$ and 7 moles of $B_2(g)$ are reacted in following manner.
$A_2(g)+3 B_2(g) \longrightarrow 2 A B_3(g)$
What is the total number of moles of the gases present in the container at the end of the reaction?
questions.solution:
Thus 1 mole of $A_2$ react with 3 mole of $B_2$
$\therefore 7$ moles of $B_2$ will react with $A_2=\frac{7}{3}$ moles
$A_2$ left $=5-\frac{7}{3}=\frac{8}{3}$ moles
1 mole of $A_2$ produces 2 moles of $A B_3$
$\therefore \frac{7}{3}$ moles of $A_2$ will produce $A B_3=\frac{7}{3} \times 2=\frac{14}{3}$ moles
$\therefore$ Total moles of gases in vessel $=\frac{8}{3}$ moles of $A_2+\frac{14}{3}$ moles of $A B_3=\frac{22}{3}$ moles

questions.q: The ionisation energy of hydrogen atom is 13.6 eV . The ionisation energy of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ ion will be
questions.solution:
For hydrogen like particle, energy of $n^{\text {th }}$-orbital is given as,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & E_n=-\frac{2 \pi^2 m Z e^4}{n^2 h^2} \text { or }-\frac{K Z^2}{n^2} \\ \\ & Where, K=\frac{2 \pi^2 m e^4}{h^2} \\ \end{aligned}$
Ionisation energy, IE = Energy at infinity - Energy at $n=1$
$\mathrm{IE}=0-\left[-\frac{K Z^2}{1^2}\right]=K Z^2$
For $\mathrm{H}, \mathrm{Z}=1$

For $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}, Z=3, \quad \mathrm{IE}=K \times 9=122.4 \mathrm{eV}$

questions.solution:
We have $\mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & b=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \\ & c=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Vector along $a-b+c=\lambda(a-b+c)$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\lambda(\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}+\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ \\ & =\lambda(-\hat{\mathbf{k}})=-\lambda \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Unit vector along $a-b+c= \pm\left(\frac{a-b+c}{|a-b+c|}\right)$
$= \pm\left(\frac{-\lambda \hat{\mathbf{k}}}{\lambda}\right)= \pm \hat{\mathbf{k}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When an alternating voltage source $V=100 \sin \left(100 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is applied to a pure capacitor of $1 \mu \mathrm{~F}$, then the instantaneous value of current through capacitor is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \\ & V=100 \sin \left(100 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\ \\ & \therefore \phi_1=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ \end{aligned}$
Since, alternating current leads $\frac{\pi}{2}$ angle from alternating voltage in purely capacitive circuit, hence phase angle of alternating current,
$\phi_2=\frac{\pi}{2}-\phi_1=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}$
$\therefore$ Instantaneous value of alternative current,
$\begin{aligned} \\ i & =i_0 \sin \left(100 \pi t+\phi_2\right) \\ \\ & =V_0 \omega C \sin \left(100 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ \\ & =100 \times 100 \pi \times 1 \times 10^{-6} \sin \left(100 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ \\ & =0.01 \pi \sin \left(100 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A step down transformer is used to reduce the main supply of 220 V to 10 V . If the primary draws 5 A and secondary 88 A current, calculate the efficiency of the transformer.
questions.solution:
$e_p=220 \mathrm{~V}, e_s=10 \mathrm{~V}, I_p=5 \mathrm{~A}$ and $I_s=88 \mathrm{~A}$
Input power, $P_i=e_P \times I_P=220 \times 5=1100 \mathrm{~W}$
Output power, $P_o=e_s \times I_s=10 \times 88=880 \mathrm{~W}$
Efficiency, $\eta=\frac{P_0}{P_1}=\frac{880}{1100}=0.8$ or $80 \%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Output of an $A C$ source is $V=100 \sin 100 \pi t \cos100 \pi t$. Which of these are correct?
options: Peak voltage of source is 100 V
Peak voltage of source is 50 V
Frequency of the source is 50 Hz
questions.solution:
The given output voltage can be written as
$\begin{aligned} \\ V=100 \sin & 100 \pi t \cos 100 \pi t \\ \\ & =50 \times 2 \sin 100 \pi t \cos 100 \pi t \\ \\ & =50 \sin 2(100 \pi t) \quad[\because 2 \sin A \cos A=\sin 2 A] \\ \\ & =50 \sin 200 \pi t \\ \end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Peak voltage of given AC source,
$V_0=50 \mathrm{~V}$
$\therefore$ Angular frequency,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & w=2 \pi f=200 \pi \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad & f=\frac{200 \pi}{2 \pi}=100 \mathrm{~Hz} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Calculate the radius of the second Bohr's orbit of electron of hydrogen atom.
questions.solution:
Radius of the $n$th Bohr's orbit of the hydrogen atom is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ r_n & =\frac{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 n^2 h^2}{4 \pi^2 m e^2} \\ \\ r_2 & =\frac{4 \pi \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times(2)^2 \times\left(6.625 \times 10^{-34}\right)^2}{4 \pi^2 \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times\left(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)^2} \\ \\ & =\frac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 4 \times\left(6.625 \times 10^{-34}\right)^2}{\pi \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times\left(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)^2} \\ \\ & =2.12 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m} \\ \\ & =2.12 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a helium ion, if potential energy of electron in ground state is assumed to be zero, then its energy in first excited state is equal to
questions.solution:
Potential energy of a $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ion in ground state is
$\begin{aligned} \\ & U_1=2 E_1=2\left(-13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\right) \\ \\ & \because \quad n=1 \text { and } Z=2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad U_1=-108.8 \mathrm{eV} \\ \end{aligned}$
But PE in ground state is given zero. So, we have to increase PE (and total energy) by 108.8 eV .
Hence, for given $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ion, energy of first excited state $(n=2)$ will be
$\begin{aligned} \\ E(n=2) & =-13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}+108.8 \\ \\ & =-13.6 \times \frac{4}{4}+108.8 \\ \\ & =95.2 \mathrm{eV} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The minimum radial distance between first orbit and second orbit in $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ion, if the de-Broglie wavelength of an electron in first orbit is $\lambda$, will be
questions.solution:
By de-Broglie hypothesis,
$2 \pi r_n=n \lambda$
For first orbit, $n=1, r=r_1$, then
$2 \pi r_1=\lambda \text { or } r_1=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi}$
For second orbit, $n=2, r=r_2$, then
$\begin{aligned} \\ 2 \pi r_2 & =2 \lambda \\ \\ \text{or } r_2 & =\frac{2 \lambda}{2 \pi} \\ \end{aligned}$
Minimum radial distance between first orbit and second orbit is
$\begin{aligned} \\ & r_2-r_1=\frac{2 \lambda}{2 \pi}-\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad & r_2-r_1=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $5.80 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ parallel plate air capacitor has a plate separation of 5 mm and is charged to a potential difference of 400 V . The energy density in the region between the plates is
questions.solution:
The energy density in the region between the plates is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ u & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2 \\ \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0\left(\frac{V}{d}\right)^2 \quad\left(\because E=\frac{V}{d}\right) \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad u & =\frac{1}{2} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times\left(\frac{400}{5 \times 10^{-3}}\right)^2 \\ \\ & =283.2 \times 10^{-12} \times 10^6 \\ \\ & =283.2 \times 10^{-6} \\ \\ & =2.83 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^3 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A capacitor of $2 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ is charged as shown in the figure. When the switch $S$ is turned to position 2 , the percentage of its stored energy dissipated is
questions.solution:

Therefore, % loss of energy
$=\frac{1.6}{2} \times 100=80 \%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A battery of emf 12 V and negligible resistance is connected across the diagonally opposite corners of a cubical network consisting of 12 resistors each of resistance $2 \Omega$. The equivalent resistance of the network is
questions.solution:
In a closed loop, say $A B C C^{\prime} E A$ and apply Kirchhoffs second rule, $-I R-\left(\frac{I}{2}\right) R-I R+\varepsilon=0$

where, $R$ is the resistance of each edge and $\varepsilon$ the emf of battery.
Thus, $\varepsilon=\frac{5}{2} I R$
The equivalent resistance $R_{\text {eq }}$ of the network is
$R_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\varepsilon}{3 I}=\frac{5}{6} R=\frac{5}{6} \times 2=\frac{5}{3} \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistor of resistance $R$ is connected to 25 V supply and heat produced in it is $25 \mathrm{Js}^{-1}$. The value of $R$ is
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{H}{t}=25 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{s}=25 \mathrm{~W} \\ \\ & V=25 \mathrm{~V} \\ \end{aligned}$
We know that,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & H=\frac{V^2}{R} t \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \frac{H}{t}=\frac{V^2}{R} \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad & 25=\frac{25^2}{R} \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad & R=\frac{25^2}{25}=25 \Omega \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the length of a wire is increased by $20 \%$ by stretching it, then its resistance is increased to
questions.solution:
Given
$\begin{aligned} \\ & l_1=l, A_1=A \\ \\ & l_2=l\left(1+\frac{20}{100}\right)=\frac{6 l}{5}, A_2=A^{\prime} \\ \end{aligned}$
We have,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & A_1 l_1=A_2 l_2 \\ \\ & A l=A^{\prime} \frac{6 l}{5} \Rightarrow A^{\prime}=\frac{5 A}{6} \\ \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{R_2}{R_1}=\frac{\frac{\rho_2}{A_2}}{\frac{\rho_1}{A_1}}=\frac{l_2}{l_1} \cdot \frac{A_1}{A_2}=\frac{\frac{6 l}{5}}{l} \cdot \frac{6}{5 \mathrm{~A}}=\frac{36}{25} \\ \end{aligned}$
Increase in the resistance,
$\left(\frac{R_2}{R_1}-1\right) \times 100=\left(\frac{36}{25}-1\right) \times 100=44 \%$

questions.q: The drift velocity of free electrons in a conducting wire is the order of $10^{-4} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Yet, the bulb glows very quickly after the switch is put ON because
options: the random speed of electrons is very high of order of $10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
the electrons transfer their energy very quickly through collisions
electric field is set-up in the wire with a speed of light producing a current through each cross-section, almost instantaneously
the random speed of electrons is very low of order of $10^{-6} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

Hence, the bulb glows very quickly.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a beam of 10.6 eV photons of intensity $2.0 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{m}^2$ falls on a platinum surface of area $1.0 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$ and work function 5.6 eV . $0.53 \%$ of the incident photons eject photoelectrons. The number of photoelectrons emitted per second is
questions.solution:
Energy of incident photons,
$\begin{aligned} \\ E_1 & =10.6 \mathrm{eV}=10.6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J} \\ \\ & =16.96 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J} \\ \end{aligned}$
Energy incident per unit area per unit time (intensity) $=2 \mathrm{~J}$
$\therefore$ Number of photons incident on unit area in unit time
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{2}{16.96 \times 10^{-19}} \\ \\ & =1.18 \times 10^{18} \\ \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} \\ \left(1.0 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2\right) & \\ \\ & =\left(1.18 \times 10^{18}\right)\left(1.0 \times 10^{-4}\right) \\ \\ & =1.18 \times 10^{14} \\ \end{aligned}$
But only $0.53 \%$ of incident, photons emit photoelectrons.
$\therefore$ Number of photoelectrons emitted per second,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & n=\left(\frac{0.53}{100}\right)\left(1.18 \times 10^{14}\right) \\ \\ & n=6.25 \times 10^{11} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with a speed of $2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. The relative permeability of the medium is 1 . The value of relative permittivity of medium is
questions.solution:
Given, $v=2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ and $\mu_r=1$
The speed of EM waves in a medium is given by
$v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}}$...(i)
where, $\mu$ and $\varepsilon$ are absolute permeability and absolute perimittivity of the medium.
Now, $\mu=\mu_0 \mu_r$ and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r$
$\therefore$ Eq. (i) becomes
$\begin{aligned} \\ & v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \mu_r \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}} \\ \\ & v=\frac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}} \\ \\ & \varepsilon_r=\frac{c^2}{v^2 \mu_r}=\frac{\left(3 \times 10^8\right)^2}{\left(2 \times 10^8\right)^2 \times 1}=2.25 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two unlike charges of the same magnitude $Q$ are placed at a distance $d$. The intensity of the electric field at the middle point is the line joining the two charges is
questions.solution:
The magnitude of electric field due to charge at point $A$ is

$E_A=|\mathbf{E}|=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{Q}{\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{4 Q}{d^2}$
Similarly, $E_B=|\mathbf{E}|=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{Q}{\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{4 Q}{d^2}$
From figure, it is clear that $E_A$ and $E_B$ are in same direction, hence.
Net electric field,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & E=E_A+E_B=2|\mathbf{E}|=2 \cdot \frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{4 Q}{d^2} \\ \\ & E=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{8 Q}{d^2} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric dipole of dipole moment $p$ is lying along a uniform electric field $E$. The work done in rotating the dipole from $60^{\circ}$ to $90^{\circ}$ from the direction of electric field, is
questions.solution:
Given, $\theta_1=60^{\circ}, \theta_2=90^{\circ}$
Work done in rotating a dipole from $\theta_1$ to $\theta_2$ in electric field is given as
$\begin{aligned} \\ W & =p E\left(\cos \theta_1-\cos \theta_2\right) \\ \\ & =p E\left(\cos 60^{\circ}-\cos 90^{\circ}\right) \\ \\ & =p E\left(\frac{1}{2}-0\right)=\frac{p E}{2} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric dipole is placed at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with an electric field intensity $10^4 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C}$. If experiences a torque equal to $4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{m}$. The charge on the dipole, if the dipole length is 1 cm , is
questions.solution:
Given, $E=10^4 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C}, \tau=4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{m}, \theta=60^{\circ}$
Dipole length, $2 l=1 \mathrm{~cm}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$
We know that, torque on dipole,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & & \tau & =p E \sin \theta \\ \\ \Rightarrow & & \tau & =2 q l E \sin \theta [\because p=2 q l]\\ \\ \Rightarrow & & 4 \sqrt{3} & =10^{-2} \cdot q \cdot 10^4 \cdot \sin 60^{\circ} \\ \\ \Rightarrow & & 4 \sqrt{3} & =10^2 \cdot q \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ \\ \Rightarrow & & q & =8 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{C}=80 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{C}=80 \mathrm{mC} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular ring of radius $r$ is placed in a homogeneous magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the ring. The field $B$ changes with time according to the equation $B=K t$, where $K$ is a constant and $t$ is the time. The electric field in the ring is
questions.solution:
$B=k t$
According to Maxwell's is equation, (Faraday's law of electro magnetic induction)
$\begin{aligned} \\ \oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d \mathbf{l} & =\frac{-d \phi_B}{d t} \\ \\ \text { or } \quad E \cdot 2 \pi r & =\frac{d}{d t}(B A) \\ \\ & =\frac{d}{d t}\left(k t \times \pi r^2\right) \left\{\therefore A=\pi r^2\right\} \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad E \cdot 2 \pi r & =k \pi r^2 \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad E & =\frac{k \pi r^2}{2 \pi r}=\frac{k r}{2} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron is moving along positive $X$-axis. To get it moving on an anti-clockwise circular path in $X-Y$-plane, a magnetic field is applied
questions.solution:
For the particle to move along anti-clockwise path, force should be along $\hat{\mathbf{j}} y$-direction.
Since, velocity is along $\hat{\mathbf{i}}$,
Hence, $F_m=-e(\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B})$
In terms of unit vectors,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \hat{\mathbf{j}}=-(\hat{\mathbf{i}} \times \hat{\mathbf{p}}) \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \hat{\mathbf{j}}=\hat{\mathbf{p}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}} \\ \end{aligned}$
Clearly, $\hat{\mathbf{p}}=\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Hence, magnetic field is applied along positive Z -axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hydraulic automobile lift is designed to lift cars with a maximum mass of 3000 kg . The area of cross-section of the piston carrying the board is $425 \mathrm{~cm}^2$. What maximum pressure would smaller piston have to bear?
questions.solution:
The maximum force, which the bigger piston can bear,
$F=30000 \mathrm{kgf}=3000 \times 9.8 \mathrm{~N}$
Area of piston,
$A=425 \mathrm{~cm}^2=425 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$
$\therefore$ Maximum pressure on the bigger piston,
$p=\frac{F}{A}=\frac{300 \times 9.8}{425 \times 10^{-4}}=6.92 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~Pa}$
Since, the liquid transmits pressure equally, therefore the maximum pressure the smaller piston can bear is $6.92 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~Pa}$

Radius of curvature, $R_1=60 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: 100 g of ice at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is mixed with 100 g of water at $80^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The final temperature of the mixture is (Given, latent heat of fusion of ice, $L_f=80 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{g}$ and specific heat capacity of water, $S_{\text {water }}=1 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{g}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ )
questions.solution:
Let the final temperature of mixture be $T^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.
From principle of calorimetry,
Heat given by 100 g of water $=$ Heat taken by 100 g of ice
$m_1 S_{\text {water }}\left(\Delta T_1\right)=m_2 L_f+m_2 S_{\text {water }} \Delta T_2$
Substituting the given values, we get
$\begin{aligned} \\ & 100 \times 1 \times(80-T)=100 \times 80+100 \times 1 \times(T-0) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 80-T=80+T \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2 T=0 \Rightarrow T=0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the coefficient of volume expansion of brass is $6 \times 10^{-5}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$, then fractional change in its density for a $60^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ rise in temperature will be
questions.solution:
Density at temperature $T$ is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ \rho & =\rho_0(1-\alpha \Delta T) \\ \\ \rho & =\rho_0-\rho_0 \alpha \Delta T \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\rho-\rho_0}{\rho_0} & =-\alpha \Delta T \\ \end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Fractional change in density,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho_0}=-\alpha \Delta T=-6 \times 10^{-5} \times 60 \\ \\ & \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho_0}=-3.6 \times 10^{-3} \\ \end{aligned}$
Note: Negative sign indicates that density decreases with rise in temperature.

From first law of thermodynamics,
$d U=d Q-d W=Q-\frac{Q}{4}=\frac{3 Q}{4}$
Now, molar heat capacity,

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, the separation between two slits is $0.3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$. When light beam is passed through the two slits, then interference pattern is observed on the screen 1.5 m away. If the first violet and red fringes are formed 2.0 mm and 3.5 mm away from the central white fringe, then the difference in wavelength of red and violet light is $x \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
In a Young's double slit experiment for interference pattern, the position of bright fringe is given by
$y_n=\frac{n \lambda D}{d}$

Here,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & D=1.5 \mathrm{~m} \\ \\ & d=0.3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m} \\ \end{aligned}$
and
$n=1 ; \lambda=\frac{y_n d}{D}$
For first violet, $y_n=2 \mathrm{~mm}=2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$
$\therefore \lambda_{\text {violet }}=2 \times 10^{-3} \frac{d}{D}$
For first red,
$\begin{aligned} \\ y_n & =3.5 \mathrm{~mm}=3.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m} \\ \\ \lambda_{\mathrm{red}} & =3.5 \times 10^{-3} \frac{d}{D} \\ \end{aligned}$
The difference in wavelengths of red and violet light is
$\begin{aligned} \\ \Delta \lambda & =\lambda_{\text {red }}-\lambda_{\text {violet }} \\ \\ & =3.5 \times 10^{-3} \frac{d}{D}-2 \times 10^{-3} \frac{d}{D} \\ \\ & =\frac{d}{D}(1.5) \times 10^{-3} \\ \\ & =\frac{0.3 \times 10^{-3}}{15} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \\ \\ & =0.3 \times 10^{-6}=0.3 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^3 \times 10^{-3} \\ \\ & =300 \times 10^{-9} \\ \\ & =x \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~m} \quad \text { (given) } \therefore x=300 \\ \end{aligned}$
